posts.text: Etter fusjon Thor Medical AS og Nordic Nanovector ASA i 2024, havnet alle patentene til gamle Nanovector i et eget elskap som heter Nuclithera AS. Thor Medical ASA har en delingsavtale der de får en % andel av et kommende overskudd om Nuclithera lykkes. Dette uten krav til ny egenkapital. Ganske unikt, og i tillegg til fremførbart underskudd på ca 3 milliarder, er dette en fremtidig asset svært få er klar over. Nå har Nuclithera lykkes med funding til et omfattende CD37 utviklingsløp basert på det gamlebpatentet. ................................................ NucliThera Awarded NOK 16 Million in Research Council Funding to Advance Next-Generation CD37-Targeted Cancer Therapy October 29, 2026 NucliThera AS is pleased to announce that the Research Council of Norway (Forskningsrådet) has approved funding for its Next-Generation CD37 project under the Innovation Project for the Industrial Sector (IPN) programme. The four-year project, with approximately NOK 16 million in public funding, will support the development of a new generation of targeted radionuclide therapies for hematological cancers. The project focuses on developing novel radioconjugates targeting CD37, a protein expressed on several types of blood cancer cells. By combining humanized antibody-based targeting molecules with lead-212 (²¹²Pb), an alpha-emitting radionuclide, NucliThera aims to develop highly targeted therapies capable of delivering potent radiation directly to malignant cells while limiting exposure to healthy tissues. Building on NucliThera’s established CD37 antibody platform and previous research, the project will focus on optimizing therapeutic candidates, improving their biological distribution and stability, and evaluating their safety and efficacy in preclinical models. The project will be conducted in collaboration with Oslo University Hospital, combining NucliThera’s expertise in radiopharmaceutical development with established capabilities in preclinical cancer research. Its objective is to identify and characterize a lead therapeutic candidate and generate the preclinical evidence and manufacturing documentation needed to support future clinical development. “This funding represents an important milestone for NucliThera and a strong recognition of the scientific and therapeutic potential of our CD37 platform. It allows us to accelerate the development of next-generation radiopharmaceuticals while strengthening our collaboration with leading Norwegian research institutions,” said Roy Larsen, Chairman of the Board and Chief Technology Officer of NucliThera. The award further strengthens NucliThera’s research and development portfolio and supports the company’s long-term strategy of advancing innovative targeted radionuclide therapies toward clinical application. About NucliThera AS: NucliThera is an R&D company developing targeted radionuclide therapies for cancer, including lymphoma and leukaemia.
